questions.prompt: In SQLite WAL mode, which concurrency pattern is supported under ordinary conditions?
questions.correct: Readers and one writer can proceed concurrently
wrong: Only one reader can be connected
Each read blocks all writes until its connection closes
Multiple independent writers can commit at the same instant

questions.prompt: In SQLite WAL mode, can two independent connections both hold the write lock at the same instant?
questions.correct: No; there is still only one writer at a time
wrong: Yes; WAL permits an unlimited number of simultaneous writers
Yes; as long as they touch different rows
Yes; if every connection uses autocommit

questions.prompt: In SQLite WAL mode, a long-running read transaction remains open while writers keep committing. What may happen to checkpoint progress?
questions.correct: The long reader can prevent a checkpoint from completing, allowing the WAL to grow
wrong: All writers are forced to stop as soon as a reader starts
Checkpointing always deletes the active reader's snapshot
The reader must automatically change to the newest snapshot

questions.prompt: A reader begins a transaction in WAL mode and sees value 10. Another connection commits value 20. The first reader queries again inside its original read transaction. What should it see?
wrong: 20 immediately, because WAL has no read snapshots
An arbitrary mix of 10 and 20
No rows, because writers invalidate all readers

questions.prompt: Which property does SQLite WAL mode provide to a read transaction?
questions.correct: A consistent database snapshot as of the transaction's read view
wrong: A view of uncommitted writes from all other connections
Guaranteed simultaneous commits by many writers
Automatic refresh of every query to the newest committed version

questions.prompt: Connection A starts reading a WAL database. Connection B then commits a change. Without ending A's read transaction, what view does A retain?
questions.correct: The snapshot from before B's commit
wrong: It switches immediately to B's new committed version
It is forced to roll back whenever B commits
It sees B's uncommitted data first

questions.prompt: In SQLite WAL mode, connection A begins a read transaction, connection B commits a change, and then A tries to upgrade that stale read transaction into a write transaction. What can SQLite return?
wrong: SQLITE_OK with an automatic merge of both snapshots
SQLITE_NOTADB because any concurrent writer corrupts WAL
SQLITE_DONE meaning all writes were committed

questions.prompt: After SQLITE_BUSY_SNAPSHOT on a stale WAL read-to-write upgrade, which approach obtains a fresh snapshot for a new write attempt?
questions.correct: Roll back the stale transaction and start a new transaction
wrong: Keep retrying the same stale transaction without ending it
Disable foreign keys and use the old transaction
Rewrite the WAL file directly from the application

questions.prompt: What is the main purpose of a SQLite WAL checkpoint?
questions.correct: Copy committed changes from the WAL into the main database file
wrong: Convert every SQL query into a prepared statement
Replace all indexes with table scans
Encrypt the WAL using the server certificate

questions.prompt: Does a successful SQLite WAL checkpoint necessarily make the WAL file disappear from the filesystem immediately?
questions.correct: No; checkpointing and removing or truncating the WAL file are distinct behaviors
wrong: Yes; every checkpoint must delete the WAL file
Yes; otherwise no committed transaction remains durable
No; because checkpointing never touches the main database file

questions.prompt: A passive WAL checkpoint encounters a reader that still needs old WAL frames. Which outcome is possible?
questions.correct: It checkpoints what it safely can without completing all frames
wrong: It overwrites the reader's active snapshot in place
It always blocks until the reader exits
It irrevocably aborts all reader transactions

questions.prompt: A SQLite application observes WAL growth during sustained long-lived reads. Which intervention targets the actual reason a checkpoint cannot fully reset the log?
questions.correct: End or shorten old read transactions so their WAL snapshots can be released
wrong: Increase SQL column-name lengths
Issue more SELECTs inside the same long-lived read transaction
Set all HTTP requests to keep-alive
